title: Working with Fractions: Multiplying and Dividing Fractions
seo_title: Working with Fractions Class 7 Worksheet with Answers (Ganita Prakash Part 1, Chapter 8)
standard_code: Class 7, Ganita Prakash Part 1, Chapter 8: Working with Fractions
standard_text: Multiplication of fractions ('of' means ×), multiplying by whole numbers, reciprocals, division of fractions and problems (summary of NCERT Ganita Prakash Class 7)
meta_desc: Class 7 Working with Fractions worksheet (Ganita Prakash Part 1, Chapter 8): fraction of a quantity, multiplying fractions, reciprocals, dividing fractions and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Multiply tops and bottoms; to divide, multiply by the reciprocal
body_html:
How it works

To multiply fractions, multiply the numerators and the denominators: 2/3 × 4/5 = 8/15. 'Of' means multiply: 3/4 of 20 = 15.

The reciprocal of 3/5 is 5/3. To divide by a fraction, multiply by its reciprocal: 3/4 ÷ 1/8 = 3/4 × 8 = 6.

Change mixed numbers to improper fractions before multiplying or dividing.

Example

Work out 2/5 × 15.

15 ÷ 5 × 2

Answer: 6

Example

Work out 2/3 ÷ 4/9.

2/3 × 9/4 = 18/12

Answer: 1 1/2

Common mistakes

  • Multiplying only the numerators.
  • Turning the first fraction upside down when dividing.
  • Multiplying the whole parts and the fraction parts of mixed numbers separately.

faq.a: Multiply the numerators together and the denominators together, then simplify.

faq.q: How do you divide by a fraction?
faq.a: Multiply by its reciprocal: a/b ÷ c/d = a/b × d/c.

faq.q: Why does dividing by 1/4 make a number bigger?
faq.a: Because you are counting how many quarters fit, and there are 4 quarters in every whole.
